newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 29.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 29.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

ANZ announced a stronger than expected 24 percent rise in pre-abnormal net profit for the first half on Wednesday and raised its dividend to 22 cents from 18 cents. ANZ CEO Don Mercer, who announced he would retire later this year, later said he saw an improved full year profit, driven in large part by a significant cut to core costs in the second half. However ANZ said housing margins had tightened further since March 31 and local profit growth would be slower than in the first half.

Standard & Poor's lowered its claims-paying ability ratings of the principal AXA S.A. insurance operating companies to double-'A'-minus from double-'A' overnight. S&P also lowered to double-'A'-minus from double-'A', the claims-paying ability ratings of its 51 percent-owned Australasian subsidiaries, National Mutual Life Association.

Australia planned to ease tough media ownership limits in a move that could allow media tycoons Kerry Packer and Rupert Murdoch to expand their empires and foreigners to take bigger media stakes, newspapers said on Thursday. The plan would allow a single proprietor to own one newspaper and one television station in the major cities of Sydney and Melbourne and would raise foreign ownership limits to 25 percent from 15 percent.

Canadian media group CanWest Global Communications Corp is set to sell an 18.5 percent stake in Australia's Ten television network to Telecasters North Queensland (TNQ) Ltd, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Thursday. The government has ruled CanWest must cut its 76 percent stake in Ten down to a previously sanctioned level of 57.5 percent.
The release of Fox's "Titanic," the movie about the ill-fated liner, has been put back six months, fueling rumors it is struggling to avoid more financial and artistic icebergs.

Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Wednesday its BHP Steel unit planned to sell the refractory product manufacturing group following a review of operations. BHP also said a liquid hydrocarbons discovery in Algeria flowed 5,570 barrels of oil a day (bopd) from a 44/46 inch choke and tested 42 degrees API crude.

Sporting goods retailer Rebel Sports Ltd said on Wednesday that the Singapore-based retailer World of Sports owned by the Goh brothers would acquire a 19.9 percent stake. The company said the remaining 8.1 percent stake in the company formerly held by founding shareholders Sam Linz and Robert Gavshon would be sold to Rebel's joint managing directors Ian Dresner and Hilton Seskin.
